final_text:
Confirming an order now books a shipment through `CarrierGateway`, stores the tracking number on the order, and exposes it on `OrderSummary`. The test suite passes.

- **`Order`**: new nullable `trackingNumber` field with a getter and an `assignTrackingNumber` setter.
- **`OrderSummary`**: new `trackingNumber()` String component, added last. It is null until a shipment is booked.
- **`OrderService`**: now takes a `CarrierGateway`. `confirm` calls `carrier.book(orderId)` before changing the status, so a carrier failure leaves the order `PLACED` with no tracking number. `OrderFacade.confirm` is still the entry point.
- **Tests**: a new `OrderServiceTest` with a fake carrier covers booking and storing the number, a failed booking leaving the order unconfirmed, and a second `confirm` not booking again.

I added one behaviour you didn't ask for: `confirm` skips the carrier call when the order already has a tracking number. Without that guard, a repeated confirm would book a second shipment.

The existing Spring flow test doesn't call `confirm`, so nothing in it touches the real `HttpCarrierGateway` URL. Anything that confirms an order through the full context will make a real HTTP call to `carrier.example`.

Baseline is green. Two things I noticed before editing:

- `OrderService.confirm` currently only flips the status. Calling the carrier there means a second `confirm` would book a second shipment, so I'll make confirm book only when no tracking number exists yet.
- `HttpCarrierGateway` calls a real URL. The existing Spring flow test doesn't call `confirm`, so I'll test the confirm path with a fake gateway at the service level rather than through the full context.
